enhanced_information: Hyperacute rejection of a transplant is primarily caused by preformed antibodies that lead to immediate recognition of the transplant as foreign, resulting in hyperacute rejection with 95% confidence. CD8 + T lymphocytes can also contribute through direct cytotoxic attack, leading to hyperacute rejection with 80% confidence. Circulating immune complexes, although involved in the activation of the complement cascade, are not the primary cause of hyperacute rejection.
